en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes,
Section on the Earth.
8. The Question on the Seven Attributes of the Sun “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘seven attributes of the sun should be adopted,’ which are those seven attributes that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the sun dries up all water;”
In the same way, Great King, all defilements must be dried up without remainder by the yogi, the practitioner of yoga.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the sun that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the sun dispels the darkness.

In the same way, Great King, the yogi, the practitioner of yoga, must dispel all the darkness of lust, the darkness of hatred, the darkness of delusion, the darkness of conceit, the darkness of views, the darkness of the defilements, and all the darkness of misconduct.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the sun that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the sun moves constantly.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga must constantly apply wise attention.
This, Great King, is the third quality of the sun that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the sun is garlanded with rays.
In the same way, Great King, the yogin practicing yoga must become one who possesses a garland of objects of focus.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of the sun that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the sun moves about scorching the great masses of people.

In the same way, Great King, the yogin, the practitioner of yoga, by means of conduct, virtue, qualities, and the performance of duties, and through the meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, attainments, faculties, powers, factors of enlightenment, foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, and bases of psychic power,
should cause the world with its devas to burn with heat.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of the sun that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the sun moves about out of fear of Rāhu; even so, Great King,
when a practitioner, a follower of yoga, sees beings who are entangled in the net of defilements— the ripening of misconduct, miserable rebirths,
and uneven wildernesses, fallen into ruin, and ensnared by the trap of wrong views— then with great agitation and fear, [he reflects].
The mind must be stirred with urgency.
This, Great King, is the sixth quality of the sun that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the sun reveals both the beautiful and the ugly.

In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, should demonstrate the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, and both mundane and supramundane states.
This, Great King, is the seventh quality to be taken from the sun.
And this, Great King, was said by the Elder Vaṅgīsa:
"Just as the rising sun reveals forms to living beings,
both the pure and the impure,"
Whether good or even evil—
so too, a monk who upholds the Dhamma [perceives] people shrouded by ignorance.
"He shows the various paths,
just like the rising of the sun. Thus ends the eighth inquiry, the Question on the Limbs of the Sun.
